Commentary.Commentary: Well, in their entire ODI history, West Indies' highest successful run chase has been 300/3, against the Proteas in Centurion, way back in 2004. With no Gayle, Dwayne Bravo and Russell, hard to see them scoring 44 runs more than that total today but cricket is a game of uncertainties. If they plan their chase well, we might get a game on our hands. South Africa, on the other hand, will aim to restrict the Windies to 274 or less to go on top of the points table for a bonus point win. Join us back at 0245 IST (2115 GMT, previous day).

It was a poor bowling performance and an abject fielding display by the Windies. Taylor was expensive and so were the rest. Narine was economical but if you actually look closely, he was by no means threatening. The South Africans just played him out. There were rumours of Sulieman Benn being injured in West Indies' last game against Australia. Perhaps that is the reason Holder gave him only 7 overs today.

A good start always lays a good platform and the 182-run stand between Amla and de Kock did just that. Amla was fluent, with a brilliant century while de Kock was slow, but was instrumental in that massive partnership. There was a minor hiccup when both fell in quick succession but then the others played wonderful cameos around Faf du Plessis, who held the innings together with a 50-ball 73, staying unbeaten. The real momentum shift came in the last 6 overs, where the Proteas amassed 82 for the loss of just AB de Villiers.

This is the first score of 300 or more in this series and South Africa have crossed that landmark in some style. After struggling for a major portion of the tournament with the bat, they have produced not only theirs, but one of the best batting displays overall in the tournament. Superb stuff.

The players are out in the middle. Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock are the openers for the Proteas. Jerome Taylor has the first new ball in his hand. Amla to face. Here we go...

AB DE VILLIERS says that he would have batted first too. But looking at the last game, he might have fielded first as well. Now, given that they have been forced to bat first, he believes that the pitch looks a good one to bat upon and his batsmen should make use of the same. Laments a couple of dropped catches in the last game and says that they conceded 20-30 runs on the field. Feels that through the years, South Africa's strength has been their top 4 batsmen, then a couple of all-rounders and then the bowlers. Informs that Phangiso has been rested and Tabraiz Shamsi comes in his place. The other change is the inclusion of Chris Morris who is fit and he replaces Kyle Abbott.

JASON HOLDER says that the pitch looks a good one to bat upon and should not change much. Says it means a lot to beat Australia and stresses for consistency. Informs that they have the same team as the last game.
Toss - It is time for the spin of the coin. Heads is the call from AB de Villiers but it is a Tail. WEST INDIES ELECT TO CHASE.
WEATHER - It is bright and sunny at Basseterre and the forecast looks very promising.

It is Game number 6 of the tri-series and the last one at St Kitts. West Indies take on South Africa in their second encounter of the series. The Proteas are at the bottom of the points table and need to win this one to stay alive. Not that they will not make the final if they lose this, but then they will make things difficult for themselves.
